comparison: Perfect match on C12 and C13. Both recognize these as methodological observations about coarse-graining effects on community member counts. OpenEval provides quantitative detail while peer review notes these were not challenged.

Perfect match on C14 and C15. Both agree that gamma distribution describes AFDs across taxonomic scales. OpenEval emphasizes the invariance pattern, while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this finding without concerns.

Perfect match on C25-C29. Both confirm successful predictions across environments and superiority over UNTB. Peer reviewers explicitly state authors showed the distribution predicted mean diversity and richness at all scales.

Perfect match on C30-C32. Both agree on failure of independence assumption and necessity of including covariance. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly discusses underestimation of variation and role of correlations.
Perfect match on C42-C45. Both agree UNTB fails as null model and SLM is superior. Peer reviewers make strong statements about UNTB inadequacy and editor confirms SLM is more appropriate choice.
Perfect match on C50-C53. Both support summary conclusions about self-similarity and differential requirements for richness vs diversity. Peer reviewers describe this as valuable and convincing work.
Perfect match on C62-C65. Both support mechanistic interpretations about interactions. Peer Reviewer 2 aligns with interpretation that correlations suggest interactions are driving force.

Strong overlap on C16-C18. Both support successful mean occupancy prediction and failure for variance. OpenEval includes C19 (error analysis) not explicitly mentioned in peer review, but peer reviewers acknowledge the model's strengths and limitations.

Strong overlap on C54-C57. Both support critique of prior work and interpretation that richness slopes don't require interactions. OpenEval includes these claims while peer review discusses sample size effects on richness correlations. Peer review doesn't explicitly address C58 which OpenEval covers separately.

Strong overlap on C8-C11 and C60-C61. Both support rationale for SLM over UNTB as null model. OpenEval treats these as background (R20) while peer review emphasizes this as central argument. Peer review provides stronger endorsement of this methodological choice.

Moderate overlap on C33-C37 regarding richness slope distributions. OpenEval R7 focuses on these claims while peer R5 covers broader set including C38-C41. Both agree on findings about positive slopes and ability to explain previously novel patterns.

Moderate overlap on C38-C41 regarding richness slope predictions. OpenEval R8 focuses on these specific predictions while peer R5 covers broader context including C33-C37. Both support successful prediction without requiring variance.

Partial overlap on C46-C47. Both address failure to predict diversity slopes without correlations. Peer R7 also covers C48-C49 (which OpenEval addresses in R11). Both agree on fundamental difference between richness and diversity patterns.

Partial overlap on C48-C49. Both support necessity of correlations for diversity predictions and mechanistic interpretation of interactions. Peer R7 also covers C46-C47 (which OpenEval addresses in R10). Agreement on role of interactions.

Minimal overlap on C58 only. Both support interpretation that evenness requires interactions. OpenEval focuses solely on C58 while peer R10 covers broader set C54-C58. Both agree on mechanistic interpretation.

Partial overlap on C60-C61. Both support argument against UNTB as appropriate null model. OpenEval R15 focuses on C59-C61 while peer R8 covers broader methodological argument including C8-C11. Strong agreement on this key point.
